entities.summary:
Discovery Records was an independent American record label that specialized in jazz and related genres — operating primarily in the late 20th century as a dedicated jazz label that documented significant jazz artists and performances for the recorded catalog, contributing to the preservation and documentation of American jazz music during a period when many major labels were reducing their jazz commitments in favor of more commercially mainstream genres.

Independent jazz labels have played a crucial role in jazz music history: from Blue Note (founded 1939), Prestige (1949), Riverside (1953), and Impulse! (1960) in the classic era, through Contemporary, Fantasy, and smaller labels in later decades — independent labels have provided the commercial infrastructure for recording jazz music that the major corporate labels were often unwilling to provide when jazz was not commercially dominant. Discovery Records fits within this tradition of independent labels serving the jazz ecosystem.

The label's catalog contributes to the documentation of jazz performance in the later 20th century — a period when jazz had moved from popular music to art music, with a smaller but dedicated audience. Independent labels like Discovery Records provided the commercial infrastructure for jazz musicians to record and reach that dedicated audience, serving the important archival and cultural function of documenting American jazz heritage.
